plugin.name: Transform Sensor

plugin.name: Destination Sensor
plugin.description:
The Destination Sensor is used to set an initial pose or a destination pose of an attached agent for Navigation2 stack via python API scripts. The sensor publishes to ROS and ROS2 using the `geometry_msgs/PoseStamped` message type.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#destination-sensor for more details.

plugin.name: Depth Camera Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns an image where the shades on the grey-scale correspond to the depth of objects.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#depth-camera for more details.

plugin.name: Control Calibration Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs control calibration criteria collected by AD Stacks (Apollo, Autoware). It generates steering, throttle or brakes with gear commands between minimum and maximum of velocity during duration.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#control-calibration for more details.

plugin.name: Color Camera Sensor
plugin.description:
This is the type of sensor that would be used for the Main Camera in Apollo.
Color Camera also has multiple post processing sensor effects that can be added to the Postprocessing field in params. Effects can be combined with an array of Postprocessing fields but order is hard coded.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#color-camera for more details.

plugin.name: Apollo Perception Visualizer 3D Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor will visualize bounding boxes on objects as detected by Apollo Stack. It does not publish any data and instead subscribes to a topic from Apollo perception module. The color of the boxes are:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#apollo-perception-visualizer-3d for more details.

plugin.name: 2D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs an image where objects are encased in a box. The color of the box depends on the type of object.
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#2d-ground-truth for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: CAN Bus Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor sends data about the vehicle chassis. The data includes:
	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

	]

	]

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: Transform Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is specifically used to parent other sensors. For example, if there is a cluster of sensors, a Transform sensor can be added at the location of the cluster and then the individual sensors can have a transform that is relative to the location of the Transform sensor.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#transform-sensor for more details.

		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: Transform Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is specifically used to parent other sensors. For example, if there is a cluster of sensors, a Transform sensor can be added at the location of the cluster and then the individual sensors can have a transform that is relative to the location of the Transform sensor.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#transform-sensor for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#3d-ground-truth for more details.

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

	]

plugin.name: Signal Sensor

		"Red": "Red"
	]

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: Transform Sensor
plugin.description:

See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#transform-sensor for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge

ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

This sensor sends data about the vehicle chassis. The data includes:
	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Device Sensor
plugin.description:

plugin.name: GPS Odometry Sensor

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#3d-ground-truth for more details.

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

bridge.name: CyberRT
bridge.description: This bridge allows connections to Apollo 5.0. CyberRT Bridge requires IP address, port number while setting up Simulation Configuration.

plugin.name: CAN Bus Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor sends data about the vehicle chassis. The data includes:
	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Device Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-device for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Odometry Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates and the vehicle velocity.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-odometry for more details.

plugin.name: GPS-INS Status Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the status of the GPS correction due to INS. The Simulator is an ideal environment in which GPS is always corrected.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-ins-status for more details.

plugin.name: IMU Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor output at a fixed rate of 100 Hz. IMU publishes data on topics where the 2nd topic has corrected IMU data.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#imu for more details.

plugin.name: Radar Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the objects detected by the radar. Detected objects are visualized with a box colored by their type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Agent": "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#radar for more details.

plugin.name: Lidar Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns a point cloud after 1 revolution.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#lidar for more details.

plugin.name: Color Camera Sensor
plugin.description:
This is the type of sensor that would be used for the Main Camera in Apollo.
Color Camera also has multiple post processing sensor effects that can be added to the Postprocessing field in params. Effects can be combined with an array of Postprocessing fields but order is hard coded.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#color-camera for more details.

plugin.name: Apollo Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to subscribe to the control topic of Apollo. This sensor also demonstrates how a user can check when SVL Simulator receives the first control message from the AD stack like Apollo. Based on this time, you can start the rest of the simulation or do some other interesting things.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#apollo-control for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates and the vehicle velocity.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-odometry for more details.

plugin.name: GPS-INS Status Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the status of the GPS correction due to INS. The Simulator is an ideal environment in which GPS is always corrected.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-ins-status for more details.

plugin.name: IMU Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor output at a fixed rate of 100 Hz. IMU publishes data on topics where the 2nd topic has corrected IMU data.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#imu for more details.

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#3d-ground-truth for more details.

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

plugin.name: Keyboard Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept keyboard control commands. Parameters are not required.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#keyboard-control for more details.

plugin.name: Wheel Control Sensor
plugin.description: This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept Logitech G920 wheel control commands. Parameters are not required.

plugin.name: Apollo Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to subscribe to the control topic of Apollo. This sensor also demonstrates how a user can check when SVL Simulator receives the first control message from the AD stack like Apollo. Based on this time, you can start the rest of the simulation or do some other interesting things.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#apollo-control for more details.

plugin.name: Clock Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs simulated time to ROS as rosgraph_msgs/Clock message, or to CyberRT as clock message. The only parameter to use is topic/channel name.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#clock for more details.

plugin.name: Apollo Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to subscribe to the control topic of Apollo. This sensor also demonstrates how a user can check when SVL Simulator receives the first control message from the AD stack like Apollo. Based on this time, you can start the rest of the simulation or do some other interesting things.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#apollo-control for more details.

plugin.name: Color Camera Sensor
plugin.description:
This is the type of sensor that would be used for the Main Camera in Apollo.
Color Camera also has multiple post processing sensor effects that can be added to the Postprocessing field in params. Effects can be combined with an array of Postprocessing fields but order is hard coded.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#color-camera for more details.

plugin.name: Lidar Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns a point cloud after 1 revolution.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#lidar for more details.

plugin.name: Apollo Control Sensor

plugin.name: CAN Bus Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor sends data about the vehicle chassis. The data includes:
	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Device Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-device for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Odometry Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates and the vehicle velocity.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-odometry for more details.

plugin.name: GPS-INS Status Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the status of the GPS correction due to INS. The Simulator is an ideal environment in which GPS is always corrected.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-ins-status for more details.

plugin.name: IMU Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor output at a fixed rate of 100 Hz. IMU publishes data on topics where the 2nd topic has corrected IMU data.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#imu for more details.

plugin.name: Radar Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the objects detected by the radar. Detected objects are visualized with a box colored by their type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Agent": "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#radar for more details.

plugin.name: Lidar Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns a point cloud after 1 revolution.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#lidar for more details.

plugin.name: Color Camera Sensor
plugin.description:
This is the type of sensor that would be used for the Main Camera in Apollo.
Color Camera also has multiple post processing sensor effects that can be added to the Postprocessing field in params. Effects can be combined with an array of Postprocessing fields but order is hard coded.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#color-camera for more details.

plugin.name: Keyboard Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept keyboard control commands. Parameters are not required.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#keyboard-control for more details.

plugin.name: Wheel Control Sensor
plugin.description: This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept Logitech G920 wheel control commands. Parameters are not required.

plugin.name: Apollo Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to subscribe to the control topic of Apollo. This sensor also demonstrates how a user can check when SVL Simulator receives the first control message from the AD stack like Apollo. Based on this time, you can start the rest of the simulation or do some other interesting things.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#apollo-control for more details.

bridge.name: CyberRT
bridge.description: This bridge allows connections to Apollo 5.0. CyberRT Bridge requires IP address, port number while setting up Simulation Configuration.

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the objects detected by the radar. Detected objects are visualized with a box colored by their type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Agent": "Magenta"
	]

plugin.name: Transform Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is specifically used to parent other sensors. For example, if there is a cluster of sensors, a Transform sensor can be added at the location of the cluster and then the individual sensors can have a transform that is relative to the location of the Transform sensor.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#transform-sensor for more details.

plugin.name: Stop Line Sensor
plugin.description: This sensor detects stop lines and stop line violations

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

		"Building"
	]

This sensor outputs simulated time to ROS as rosgraph_msgs/Clock message, or to CyberRT as clock message. The only parameter to use is topic/channel name.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#clock for more details.

plugin.name: IMU Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor output at a fixed rate of 100 Hz. IMU publishes data on topics where the 2nd topic has corrected IMU data.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#imu for more details.

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#3d-ground-truth for more details.

plugin.name: GPS-INS Status Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the status of the GPS correction due to INS. The Simulator is an ideal environment in which GPS is always corrected.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-ins-status for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Odometry Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates and the vehicle velocity.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-odometry for more details.

plugin.name: Keyboard Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept keyboard control commands. Parameters are not required.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#keyboard-control for more details.

plugin.name: Signal Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns ground truth data for traffic light signals connected to the current lane of ego vehicle and creates bounding boxes around the detected signals. The color of the bounding box corresponds to the signal's type:
	[
		"Green": "Green"
		"Yellow": "Yellow"
		"Red": "Red"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#signal-sensor for more details.

	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

bridge.name: ROS2ForUnitySVLBridge
bridge.description:
ROS2 For Unity svl bridge by Robotec.ai

If you are using this plugin with ADE image in Autoware.Auto (https://www.autoware.org/) project then you are good to go and don't need to do anything. Otherwise, you have to prepare your SVL simulator:

IMPORTANT #1: This bridge requires additional binaries based on your ROS2 and OS versions. Go to https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity/releases to download required archive, then extract its contents to SVL simulator:
1. libraries from `Plugins/<OS_NAME>/x86_64/*` put into `simulator_Data/Plugins` of svl simulator directory,
2. libraries from `Plugins/*.dll` put into `simulator_Data/Managed` of svl simulator directory.

IMPORTANT #2: In order for plugin to work, you have to also set "LD_LIBRARY_PATH" points to " <APP>/simulator_Data/Plugins" folder.

IMPORTANT #3: You must have your ROS2 environment sourced before running application.

This is native ROS2 bridge implementation based on ros2-for-unity project: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ros2-for-unity

Source code: https://github.com/RobotecAI/ROS2ForUnity

plugin.name: CAN Bus Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor sends data about the vehicle chassis. The data includes:
	* Speed [m/s]
	* Throttle [%]
	* Braking [%]
	* Steering [+/- %]
	* Parking Brake Status [bool]
	* High Beam Status [bool]
	* Low Beam Status [bool]
	* Hazard Light Status [bool]
	* Fog Light Status [bool]
	* Left Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Right Turn Signal Status [bool]
	* Wiper Status [bool]
	* Reverse Gear Status [bool]
	* Selected Gear [Int]
	* Engine Status [bool]
	* Engine RPM [RPM]
	* GPS Latitude [Latitude]
	* GPS Longitude [Longitude]
	* Altitude [m]
	* Orientation [3D Vector of Euler angles]
	* Velocity [3D Vector of m/s]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#can-bus for more details.

plugin.name: Keyboard Control Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is required for a vehicle to accept keyboard control commands. Parameters are not required.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#keyboard-control for more details.

plugin.name: 3D Ground Truth Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor returns 3D ground truth data for training and creates bounding boxes around the detected objects. The color of the object corresponds to the object's type:
	[
		"Car": "Green"
		"Pedestrian": "Yellow"
		"Bicycle": "Cyan"
		"Unknown":  "Magenta"
	]
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#3d-ground-truth for more details.

plugin.name: GPS Odometry Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor outputs the GPS location of the vehicle in Longitude/Latitude and Northing/Easting coordintates and the vehicle velocity.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#gps-odometry for more details.

plugin.name: Transform Sensor
plugin.description:
This sensor is specifically used to parent other sensors. For example, if there is a cluster of sensors, a Transform sensor can be added at the location of the cluster and then the individual sensors can have a transform that is relative to the location of the Transform sensor.
See https://www.svlsimulator.com/docs/simulation-content/sensors-list/#transform-sensor for more details.
